topic: Startup — Documenting the messy reality of building software solutions in public

post.topic: Startup — Documenting the messy reality of building software solutions in public
post.linkedin_text:
Nobody tells you how lonely building a startup actually gets at first.

At JAEXS Solutions, we focus on finding generic, reusable solutions for everyday problems. But some days, the hardest part isn't writing the code. It is simply showing up and sharing the messy process.

Building in public feels uncomfortable. You push code that isn't pretty. You talk about ideas that might fail. You share half-baked workflows.

→ Share the bug, not just the fix.
→ Document the failed approach, not just the architecture.
→ Talk to potential users before your landing page is live.

Perfectionism kills momentum faster than bad code ever will.

How do you keep yourself accountable when working on your own projects?

#StartupJourney #BuildInPublic #SoftwareEngineering #Solopreneur #WebDevelopment

post.threads_text:
Building JAEXS Solutions in public taught me one thing: perfectionism is just fear in disguise. 

Share the messy code. Talk about the failed approaches. Nobody cares about the highlight reel as much as the real problem-solving process.

How do you beat the urge to hide until everything is perfect?

#buildinpublic
post.instagram_caption:
Building a startup like JAEXS Solutions isn't about giant breakthroughs. It's about tackling annoying everyday problems one reusable solution at a time. 

Here is what I've learned about building in public:
• Share the bug, not just the final fix
• Document failed architectural approaches
• Talk to users before the product looks pretty
• Kill perfectionism before it kills momentum
